title: client suspend/rejoin: grace-window token + server soft-timeout mapping for OpenAI-compat
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a server-side soft-timeout mapping and a client suspend/rejoin token to the OpenAI compatibility streaming layer. Backwards compatible; default behavior unchanged. SDKs will be updated in a follow-up to surface the rejoin token to clients.
description: Motivation: Customers saw production incidents when mobile clients disconnected briefly and retried without an application-level rejoin token. Our previous approach relied on opaque stream eviction windows that were hard to map to OpenAI-compatible semantics. This PR introduces an explicit "suspend"/"rejoin" primitive in the openai-compat adapter and a server-side soft-timeout that makes graceful rejoin behavior deterministic and observable. Design summary: 1) OpenAI-compat changes: the adapter emits a 'suspend' event to clients when the connection is intentionally quiesced (server-initiated idle quiesce or graceful connection handoff). The adapter also returns a 'rejoin_token' in the final JSON meta frame (application-level header) which clients can include in a reconnect request to reattach to the same server-side session if the soft-timeout has not elapsed. 2) Server runtime: introduce 'soft_timeout_ms' for suspend windows (configurable per model/pool). While soft_timeout_ms is active the session is kept in a quarantined state (KV cache preserved); after expiration a hard eviction frees KV and compute resources. 3) Cancel semantics: a client-initiated cancel still causes an immediate server abort unless the client explicitly provides the rejoin_token and a header 'X-Resume-Intent: suspend' to request soft-suspend instead of hard-cancel. This keeps current cancel semantics by default while enabling idempotent rejoin workflows. 4) Tool/function calling safety: when a suspend is requested mid-tool-call, runtime now records call state and emits a small resume manifest (call-id + idempotency tokens) into the rejoin_token payload so the client can safely re-issue or continue the tool call on rejoin. This avoids duplicate side effects for commonly used HTTP/webhook tool integrations. Implementation highlights: - internal/streaming/lifecycle.go: new suspend/rejoin lifecycle manager with TTL and state transitions (active -> suspended -> evicted). - api/openai_compat/stream_adapter.go: wire adapter to emit suspend meta frame and include rejoin_token in the final JSON chunk. - runtime/session/quarantine_store.go: lightweight in-memory quarantined state keyed by rejoin_token; pluggable to Redis for Dedicated deployments. - docs/api/streaming.md: documents rejoin_token format, headers, and example request/response flow. - sdk/js/src/rejoin.ts (stub): client-side helper to reattach when rejoin_token is present (follow-up will publish to SDK). - tests/stream_rejoin_test.go: unit + e2e harness to simulate disconnect, short reconnect, and TTL expiration. Commits (summary): - a1d3f20: lifecycle manager + unit tests - b4c9b82: openai_compat adapter changes + integration shim - c7f2e11: docs + test harness + flake fixes
